recs.name: Mordecai
recs.shortDescription: A stylish New American restaurant and whiskey bar right in Wrigleyville, known for its extensive whiskey list alongside a refined but approachable menu. A step up from the sports-bar scene nearby.

recs.name: Pedestrian Coffee
recs.shortDescription: A bright, airy café right by the Belmont CTA stop, known for seasonal lattes and a laptop-friendly atmosphere with plenty of outlets and seating.

recs.name: Cubby Bear
recs.shortDescription: One of Wrigleyville's most iconic bars, sitting directly across from Wrigley Field — a high-energy game-day staple with multiple floors and a rowdy, celebratory atmosphere.

recs.name: Wrigley Field
recs.shortDescription: The second-oldest ballpark in Major League Baseball, famous for its ivy-covered outfield walls and hand-turned scoreboard. The whole reason most guests are staying in this neighborhood.

recs.name: Southport Corridor
recs.address: Southport Ave between W Belmont Ave and W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60657
recs.shortDescription: A charming stretch of independently owned boutiques, vintage and record shops, and bustling restaurant patios — a great walkable shopping alternative to the sports-bar-heavy Clark Street strip.

recs.name: Music Box Theatre
recs.shortDescription: A beautifully preserved historic movie palace showing indie and classic films, complete with a live organist before select showings. A one-of-a-kind evening activity for film lovers.

recs.name: Smoke Daddy
recs.shortDescription: Award-winning barbecue with a side of live blues music, long a favorite for both locals and visiting Cubs fans. Great patio seating for a laid-back meal near the ballpark.

recs.name: Bombastic Cafe
recs.shortDescription: A beloved local coffee shop known for its friendly, familiar-face service and a cozy outdoor fire pit — a warm neighborhood hangout more than a quick-stop café.

recs.name: Murphy's Bleachers
recs.shortDescription: A Wrigleyville landmark right across from the ballpark, famous for its rooftop views and electric game-day crowd. As classic a Cubs-adjacent bar experience as it gets.

recs.name: Belmont Harbor & Dog Beach
recs.shortDescription: A picturesque stretch of Lake Michigan shoreline with a marina, sailing charters, and a well-loved dog beach. A relaxing lakefront escape just minutes from the Wrigleyville buzz.

recs.name: Crosby's Kitchen
recs.shortDescription: A reliable neighborhood gastropub known for elevated comfort food and a lively weekend brunch scene. Good pick for groups who want solid food without the sports-bar noise.

recs.name: Tango Sur
recs.shortDescription: A neighborhood favorite for generous cuts of Argentinian steak at a fraction of downtown prices, with a BYOB policy guests love. A great date-night option just off the main Wrigleyville strip.

recs.name: Ann Sather
recs.shortDescription: A Chicago institution since the 1920s, famous for its homemade cinnamon rolls and hearty Swedish diner classics. A comforting, old-school breakfast stop with real neighborhood history.

recs.name: Chilam Balam
recs.shortDescription: A sustainably minded, BYOB Mexican spot serving farm-fresh small plates in a cozy basement-level space. A favorite for guests wanting something more inventive than standard tacos.

recs.name: Batter & Berries
recs.shortDescription: Known for decadent loaded french toast flights and a lively brunch crowd. One of Lakeview's most popular breakfast destinations — a great start before a day game.

recs.name: Galata Mediterranean Grill
recs.shortDescription: A neighborhood Turkish spot inspired by the historic Galata Tower, serving lahmacun, kebabs, and fresh-baked pides made from family recipes. A flavorful, casual dinner choice.

recs.name: Felix Modern American Dining
recs.shortDescription: A modern American restaurant with a seasonally driven menu and polished but unfussy atmosphere — a strong pick for guests wanting a slightly elevated dinner near Wrigley.

recs.name: Small Cheval
recs.shortDescription: A cult-favorite smash burger spot from the team behind Au Cheval, serving a compact menu of exceptional burgers and fries. Fast, casual, and dangerously good pre- or post-game.

recs.name: Coda Di Volpe
recs.shortDescription: A polished, wood-fired Italian restaurant from the Boka Restaurant Group, serving pizzas and shareable Southern Italian plates in a warm, energetic dining room.

recs.name: Uncommon Ground
recs.shortDescription: A Lakeview mainstay for over 30 years, serving organic coffee and espresso alongside a full food menu and regular live music nights — equally good for a quiet coffee or an evening out.

recs.name: Cafe Tola
recs.shortDescription: A Mexican-inspired café serving great coffee alongside empanadas and other light bites. A flavorful, laid-back stop for a coffee-and-snack break.

recs.name: Elevate Coffee
recs.shortDescription: A local coffee spot known for a smooth nitro cold brew and easygoing atmosphere — a solid quick-stop option in the Boystown/Lakeview stretch.

recs.name: Sluggers
recs.shortDescription: Part dive bar, part entertainment venue — Sluggers offers batting cages and dueling piano nights alongside the usual bar fare. A fun, interactive stop before or after the game.

recs.name: Nisei Lounge
recs.shortDescription: A true Wrigleyville dive bar — cheap drinks, zero pretension, and a loyal following of regulars and pre-game fans. The anti-rooftop-bar option for guests who want the classic bleacher-bum experience.

recs.name: Trader Todd's
recs.shortDescription: A tropical-themed beer garden and tiki bar with a seafood-forward menu, tropical cocktails, and regular karaoke nights — a fun change of pace from the sports-bar strip.

recs.name: Pilot Project Brewing - Wrigleyville
recs.shortDescription: A Wrigleyville outpost of the local Pilot Project brewery collective, pouring rotating small-batch craft beers in a casual taproom setting.

recs.name: Corridor Brewery & Provisions
recs.shortDescription: A farmhouse-style craft brewery on the Southport Corridor pairing ever-changing house beers with a locally sourced food menu — a quieter alternative to the Clark Street bar strip.

recs.name: Underground Lounge
recs.shortDescription: Wrigleyville's best-kept secret for live music, hosting local bands in an intimate, no-frills setting. A great pick for guests wanting nightlife beyond the sports-bar scene.

recs.name: Rizzo's Bar & Inn
recs.shortDescription: A longtime Lakeview bar known for live music and a relaxed, unpretentious crowd. A solid pick for guests who want a night out that isn't centered on the ballpark scene.

recs.name: Budweiser Brickhouse Tavern
recs.shortDescription: A Clark Street tavern just steps from Wrigley Field with rooftop patio seating and game-day crowds — reliable pre- or post-game energy right in the thick of it.

recs.name: Kelly Park
recs.shortDescription: A full acre of open grass and playground space that serves as Wrigleyville's go-to cooldown spot — popular with families winding down after a game or before heading into the neighborhood's energy.

recs.name: Graceland Cemetery
recs.shortDescription: A leafy, historic cemetery that's also an outdoor architecture and sculpture showcase, home to the tombs of many famous Chicagoans. A quietly fascinating stop for history-minded guests.

recs.name: Bill Jarvis Migratory Bird Sanctuary
recs.address: 3550 N DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60613
recs.shortDescription: A tucked-away lakefront sanctuary popular with birdwatchers for spotting resident and migratory species. A peaceful, free nature break within walking distance of the neighborhood.

recs.name: Laugh Factory Chicago
recs.shortDescription: A well-known stop for both emerging and established comedians, with the occasional surprise celebrity drop-in. A solid evening-out option beyond dinner and drinks.

recs.name: Dat Donut
recs.shortDescription: A beloved South Side Chicago donut institution now with a Lakeview location, famous for its oversized 'Big Dat' donut. A fun, sugary stop any time of day.

recs.name: Millennium Park & The Bean
recs.shortDescription: Home to Cloud Gate (aka 'The Bean'), Crown Fountain, and the Pritzker Pavilion — one of Chicago's most iconic and unmissable free attractions, a quick ride south of Wrigleyville.

recs.name: Chicago Riverwalk
recs.shortDescription: A 1.25-mile riverfront path lined with bars, restaurants, and boat tour docks, with great views of the city's famous architecture. A perfect half-day downtown excursion.

recs.name: Art Institute of Chicago
recs.shortDescription: One of the world's premier art museums, with an outstanding Impressionist and modern art collection alongside the iconic lion statues out front. Worth a half-day for art-loving guests.

recs.name: Navy Pier
recs.shortDescription: A lakefront entertainment pier with a giant Ferris wheel, boat cruises, and skyline views — a classic, crowd-pleasing outing for families or first-time Chicago visitors.

recs.name: Willis Tower Skydeck
recs.shortDescription: One of the tallest buildings in the Western Hemisphere, with a glass-floored 'Ledge' jutting out over the city 103 floors up. A bucket-list stop for guests wanting the full skyline view.

recs.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
recs.shortDescription: One of the few free zoos in the country, and one of the closest downtown-adjacent attractions to Wrigleyville. A great low-cost, easy-to-reach outing for families.

recs.name: Chicago Architecture Center River Cruise
recs.shortDescription: A guided boat tour along the Chicago River highlighting the city's landmark architecture, led by trained docents. Consistently rated one of the best first-time-visitor activities in the city.
